text:
- chief complaint: the patient presents with a chronic itchy, scaly scalp with dandruff-like flaking, worsening over about six months.
- history of present illness: the patient has had persistent, embarrassing scalp itching and heavy flaking for an extended period, worsening over roughly six months. No rash elsewhere on the body. Hair dye use is longstanding, with no new products. Head and Shoulders and castor oil provided no relief. No joint pain, fever, or weight loss. A sibling may have dry scalp. No recent new stressors.
- physical examination: vital signs are normal (BP 130/68, HR 98, RR 18, temperature 97.7°F). Scalp exam shows demarcated, scaly, erythematous patchy plaques diffusely across the back of the scalp.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: scalp itching, scalp flaking/dandruff, and embarrassment about visible flaking. No joint pain, fever, or weight loss.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: clobetasol 0.05% topical solution applied twice daily to affected scalp areas during flares; continue T-Gel shampoo.
- follow-up instructions: return in three months, or sooner if symptoms significantly worsen.
